title: Tehran’s Calculus: Iran’s Strategy Amidst the Storm
transcriptText:

uh machinations and maneuvers is

say.
A regime change from the air is a very

able to decentralize

offensive fire,

a lot of the targeting when you when one

elements
of the regime itself. So, targeting

do you expect a protest to resume once

power right now to the to the best sort
of degree that we can understand it

segments.text: Welcome to The Last Line of Defense. I'm Seth Jones, your host and president of the Defense and Security Department at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, and I am joined today uh honored to have Ambassador Ryan Crocker,

who served as US Ambassador to Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Syria, Kuwait, Lebanon, and I'm sure I'm forgetting some country in there, but it's a long list. Uh Ambassador Crocker, or Ryan, as I think I'll call you over the course of this discussion, really

appreciate you taking a few minutes to talk with us to uh today. >> Happy to be here, Seth. >> All right, so lots going on in the Middle East right now with the Iranians. Uh over the course of your career, you have met with Iranian officials,

including as part of your time in the US government. What is your sense, kind of where we're at with the war right now about Iran's strategy right now? And And then also as part of that, who's in charge and is making decisions? So,

what's your sense about where the Iranians are at right now? >> Well, Seth, let me start with a a major disclaimer. Iran is probably the most complex political society in the complicated Middle East, and it's by far and away the one we know the least about. We

haven't had a sustained on-the-ground presence since 1979, and our ability to uh to read uh Iranian internal uh machinations and maneuvers is extremely limited. It's what the Donald Rumsfeld would have called a known unknown.

We really don't know what's going on uh inside the regime. We do know that they uh were prepared for the attacks that they're experiencing now, they did decentralize their command and control. Uh but uh beyond that, it's very hard to say.

A regime change from the air is a very hard thing to accomplish. I think we're discovering that now. Uh and what comes next, I I couldn't guess except I think that uh for the regime to survive is to win. Uh and they are surviving as far as we can tell.
